'''Christopher Carl Singleton Jr.''' (born November 21, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Listed at 6'9" (2.06 m),<ref>[https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/players/chris-singleton/006614/ SINGLETON, CHRIS CENTER HEIGHT: 2.06.]</ref> he played as a [[power forward]] and [[small ball (basketball)|small ball]] [[center (basketball)|center]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]].

==High school career==
Singleton attended both [[Cherokee High School (Canton, Georgia)|Cherokee High School]] and [[Dunwoody High School]].

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Singleton was listed as the No. 3 small forward and the No. 12 player in the nation in 2008.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Chris-Singleton-43760;_ylt=AicpKe92QfcIioHvLtQ03_lGPZB4 Chris Singleton Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Singleton played three years of [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State University]] [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Seminoles]], where he earned [[Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball|ACC]] Defensive Player of the Year honors in 2011. After losing in the Sweet Sixteen of the [[2011 NCAA Tournament]], Singleton decided to leave FSU and declared himself eligible for the [[2011 NBA draft]].<ref name=bio>[http://www.seminoles.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=32900&ATCLID=209583258 Chris Singleton Bio]</ref>

==Professional career==
[[File:Chris Singleton Kyrie Irving Enes Kanter (7984100284).jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.7|Singleton with [[Kyrie Irving]] and [[Enes Kanter]] at the [[2011 NBA draft]]]]

On June 23, 2011, Singleton was selected by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the 18th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. On December 9, 2011, he signed with the Wizards. On March 22, 2012, he tied his career high 16 points in an 83–85 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20120322/INDWAS/gameinfo.html Notebook: Pacers 85, Wizards 83]</ref>

On September 5, 2014, Singleton signed with the Indiana Pacers.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-four-players Pacers Sign Four Free Agents]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Pacers on October 25, 2014.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-four-players Pacers Waive Four Players]</ref> On October 31, 2014, he signed with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/139514/jiangsu-dragons-cut-jarrid-famous-signing-chris-singleton.html |title=Jiangsu Dragons cut Jarrid Famous, signing Chris Singleton |access-date=2014-11-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141101061531/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/139514/jiangsu-dragons-cut-jarrid-famous-signing-chris-singleton.html |archive-date=2014-11-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In December 2014, he left Jiangsu after appearing in 17 games. On January 23, 2015, he was acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://oklahomacity.dleague.nba.com/news/150123_chris-singleton/ |title=Blue Acquires Chris Singleton |access-date=2015-01-23 |archive-date=2015-03-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150322115522/http://oklahomacity.dleague.nba.com/news/150123_chris-singleton/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On September 24, 2015, Singleton signed with the Russian team [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] for the 2015–16 season.<ref>[https://lokobasket.com/news/5153109.html Крис Синглтон подписал 1-летний контракт с "Локо"] {{in lang|ru}}</ref> In June 2016, he signed in China with the [[Anhui Dragons]] for the 2016 [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]] season,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/200873/chris-singleton-signs-with-anhui-wenyi.html |title=Chris Singleton signs with Anhui Dragons |access-date=2016-06-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160603065838/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/200873/chris-singleton-signs-with-anhui-wenyi.html |archive-date=2016-06-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> where he won the championship and was named finals MVP.<ref>[http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/461662/Anhui-celebrate-NBL-title Anhui celebrate NBL title]</ref>

On July 1, 2016, Singleton signed a one-year deal (with a team option for a second year) with Greek club [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Panathinaikos signs versatile forward Singleton|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/73nxs68iw7y6cvcr/panathinaikos-signs-versatile-forward-singleton|access-date=July 1, 2016|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 1, 2016}}</ref>

On July 17, 2018, Singleton signed a one-year deal with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona Lassa]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Agreement to sign Chris Singleton {{!}} FC Barcelona |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/sections/basketball/first-team/news/2018-2019/agreement-to-sign-chris-singleton |access-date=17 July 2018 |work=FC Barcelona |date=17 July 2018}}</ref>

On September 10, 2019, Singleton signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/chris-singleton-joins-anadolu-efes-istanbul/|title=Chris Singleton joins Anadolu Efes Istanbul|date=September 10, 2019|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 10, 2019}}</ref> On June 21, 2023, he mutually parted ways with the Turkish powerhouse after three-and-a-half successful seasons.
